I have not written `SKILL.md` yet. I am reading three files first.

1. `references/discovery.md` holds the frontmatter rules and the body template. The writing-skills skill says to read it before I write either one.
2. `references/bulletproofing.md` explains how to build the rationalization table (each excuse an agent gave, paired with a reply) and the red flags list (thoughts that mean an agent is about to skip the rule).
3. `specs/migration-dry-run-baseline.md` holds all the verbatim excuses. I only have three of them in context: "staging is disposable", "the migration is only additive", and "the dry run takes too long". The table must use the full set, word for word.

The baseline shows that agents skip a rule they already know when under pressure. So the right form is a prohibition, a rationalization table, and a red flags list. A soft "prefer a dry run" would not fit this failure.

I will also check which migration tool the scenarios used. The dry-run command in the body depends on the tool, and I will not guess it. If the baseline does not name one, I will ask you.

After the reads, I write the file. Then we run the same four scenarios with the skill present to check that agents comply.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The `description` field will state only when to use the skill, never how it works. A description that summarizes the workflow gives agents a shortcut, and they skip the body.
- Each table row will come from a real baseline excuse. An invented excuse would counter something no agent said.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
